meta.title: GQL Federation — Schema Standards and Patterns
meta.source: GQL Federation - Schema Standards and Patterns + Apollo GraphOS schema linter rules
meta.notes: House rules (source: house) come from the FedGQL standards document. Apollo GraphOS linter rules (source: apollo) use their GraphOS rule IDs; a house rule that enforces the same thing lists the GraphOS ID under 'apollo' instead of being duplicated. Rules with enforcedBy: graphos need data the registry does not model (directive definitions, unions, schema-level @contact) — they are listed for reference and checked by GraphOS at publish time.

discouraged.DateTime: Prefer DateTimeISO — a timestamp with a mandatory time-zone offset.
discouraged.LocalDateTime: Prefer DateTimeISO wherever an offset applies; LocalDateTime has no offset.

rules.title: Type names must be PascalCase
rules.message: type/enum/input/interface names must be PascalCase (e.g. ProductAvailability).
rules.fix: Rename to PascalCase, namespaced by the owning subgraph where applicable.

rules.title: Avoid all-uppercase abbreviations
rules.message: avoid all-uppercase names/abbreviations unless agreed (agreed: CTA, Org, Promo).
rules.fix: Use PascalCase; abbreviations are title-cased (Org, Promo) unless on the agreed all-caps list.

rules.title: Type names don't start with 'Type'
rules.message: type names should not start with the redundant prefix 'Type' (e.g. TypeBook).
rules.fix: Drop the prefix: type TypeBook → type Book.

rules.title: Type names don't end with 'Type'
rules.message: type names should not end with the redundant suffix 'Type' (e.g. BookType).
rules.fix: Drop the suffix: type BookType → type Book.

rules.title: Object types don't start with 'Object'
rules.message: object type names should not start with the redundant prefix 'Object' (e.g. ObjectBook).
rules.fix: Drop the prefix: type ObjectBook → type Book.

rules.title: Object types don't end with 'Object'
rules.message: object type names should not end with the redundant suffix 'Object' (e.g. BookObject).
rules.fix: Drop the suffix: type BookObject → type Book.

rules.title: Interfaces don't start with 'Interface'
rules.message: interface names should not start with the redundant prefix 'Interface' (e.g. InterfaceBook).
rules.fix: Drop the prefix: interface InterfaceBook → interface Book.

rules.title: Interfaces don't end with 'Interface'
rules.message: interface names should not end with the redundant suffix 'Interface' (e.g. BookInterface).
rules.fix: Drop the suffix: interface BookInterface → interface Book.

rules.title: Input types end with 'Input'
rules.message: input type names should follow <Operation>Input (end with 'Input'), e.g. ApplyPromoInput.
rules.fix: Name the input after the query/mutation it serves and suffix it with 'Input'.

rules.title: Object/input fields must be camelCase
rules.message: field names must be camelCase (e.g. phoneNumber).
rules.fix: Rename the field to camelCase.

rules.title: Fields don't start with REST verbs
rules.message: field and query names should not start with get, list, post, put or patch — only mutations lead with a verb.
rules.fix: Name the field after what it returns: getUsers → users.

rules.title: Boolean fields avoid is/has/can prefixes
rules.message: Boolean fields should avoid is/has/can prefixes and negative names (prefer 'active' over 'isActive').
rules.fix: Drop the prefix unless it genuinely adds clarity; avoid negative names like 'inactive'.

rules.title: Argument names must be camelCase
rules.message: argument names must be camelCase (e.g. blogPostContent, not BlogPostContent).
rules.fix: Rename the argument / parameter to camelCase.

rules.title: Entity @key fields must be non-null
rules.message: entity @key fields must be non-null (end with !).
rules.fix: Mark every field named in @key(fields: "…") as non-null, e.g. sku: ID!.

rules.title: Array fields must be non-null with non-null elements
rules.message: array fields must be non-null with non-null elements: [Type!]! (no data = empty array).
rules.fix: Write the type as [Type!]! so consumers only check for emptiness, never null.

rules.title: Enum values must be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
rules.message: enum values must be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (e.g. NEXT_DAY).
rules.fix: Uppercase the value and separate words with underscores.

rules.title: Enums don't start with 'Enum'
rules.message: enum names should not start with the redundant prefix 'Enum' (e.g. EnumResidence).
rules.fix: Drop the prefix: enum EnumResidence → enum Residence.

rules.title: Enums don't end with 'Enum'
rules.message: enum names should not end with the redundant suffix 'Enum' (e.g. ResidenceEnum).
rules.fix: Drop the suffix: enum ResidenceEnum → enum Residence.

rules.title: Input-only enums end with 'Input'
rules.message: is only used as an input (argument or input field) — enums used as inputs should end with 'Input'. Enums also returned by a field are exempt here (see ENUM_USED_AS_OUTPUT_DESPITE_SUFFIX).
rules.fix: Rename the enum with an Input suffix, e.g. enum Role → enum RoleInput.

rules.title: Output enums don't end with 'Input'
rules.message: ends with 'Input' but is returned by a field — output enums should not use the Input suffix.
rules.fix: Rename the enum without the suffix, e.g. enum RoleInput → enum Role.

rules.title: Consider an UNKNOWN enum value
rules.message: consider adding an UNKNOWN value so consumers implement catch-all handling and enum additions stay safe.
rules.fix: Add UNKNOWN as a catch-all value to the enum.

rules.title: Use a standardized custom scalar
rules.message: is not in the approved custom-scalar list — confirm it is a standardized scalar before use.
rules.fix: Use one of the curated scalars (DateTimeISO, Money, URL, UUID, …) or propose the new scalar in a schema review.

rules.title: Prefer DateTimeISO for timestamps
rules.message: prefer DateTimeISO for timestamps (it mandates a time-zone offset).
rules.fix: Replace DateTime/LocalDateTime with DateTimeISO where an offset applies.

rules.title: Use Money for monetary values
rules.message: monetary fields should use the Money scalar, not Decimal/Float (percentages/ratios/counts are exempt).
rules.fix: Change the field type to Money to signal monetary intent. Fields that are percentages, ratios, rates or counts (e.g. meatYieldCostPercent) may keep Decimal.

rules.title: Query names must be camelCase
rules.message: query names must be camelCase and namespaced (e.g. product, loyaltyPlans).
rules.fix: Rename to camelCase; use the singular for 0/1 result and plural for many.

rules.title: Mutation names must be camelCase
rules.message: mutation names must be camelCase (e.g. applyDiscountCodePromo).
rules.fix: Rename to camelCase.

rules.title: Mutations start with a domain verb
rules.message: mutation names should start with a domain verb (e.g. applyDiscountCodePromo, createDiscountSubscription).
rules.fix: Lead with a verb in business/domain language; prefer domain terms over CRUD.

rules.title: Use a single input type argument
rules.section: Use a Single Input Type Argument for Queries/Mutations
rules.message: queries/mutations should take a single input: <Name>Input argument (exempt: stable lookup-by-id queries).
rules.fix: Group arguments into one input type, e.g. products(input: ProductsInput).

rules.title: Directive names must be camelCase
rules.message: directive names must be camelCase (e.g. @specialField, not @SpecialField).
rules.fix: Rename the directive (definition and every usage) to camelCase.

rules.title: @deprecated must give a reason
rules.message: uses @deprecated without a reason argument.
rules.fix: Add a reason naming the replacement and the planned removal date, e.g. @deprecated(reason: "Use Product.name instead").

rules.title: @tag uses an approved name
rules.message: uses a @tag name that is not on the approved list (standards.json → tags.approved).
rules.fix: Use an approved @tag name, or add the name to tags.approved (and in GraphOS Studio) after review. The check is skipped while tags.approved is empty.

rules.title: Subgraph declares owner @contact
rules.message: subgraph schemas should declare owner contact details with the @contact directive on the schema.
rules.fix: Add extend schema @contact(name: "…", url: "…", description: "…") to the subgraph SDL.

rules.title: Every element has a description
rules.message: is missing a description — every type, field, enum value, operation and argument should be documented.
rules.fix: Fill the Description column, and add a """description""" line above each field / value / parameter (✎ Edit row).

rules.title: Every defined type is used
rules.message: is not referenced by any field, argument, interface or operation in the registry (entities, enums and scalars are checked separately).
rules.fix: Reference the type from a field / operation, or remove it once refactored out.

rules.title: Schemas don't declare operations
rules.message: contains an executable operation (query / mutation / subscription / fragment) — operations belong to clients, not schemas.
rules.fix: Remove the operation document from the Definition; keep only type definitions.

rules.title: SDL must parse
rules.message: is malformed SDL (unbalanced brackets/quotes or a line that is not 'name: Type').
rules.fix: Fix the syntax; each field is name(args): Type @directives on its own line.

rules.title: No field/type versioning
rules.message: avoid version suffixes like V2 — schema versioning is a GQL anti-pattern.
rules.fix: Use the 2-stage deprecation approach (@deprecated with a planned deletion date) instead of a versioned name.

rules.title: An object is an entity in every subgraph
rules.message: is declared with @key in another subgraph but as a plain type here — the supergraph gets incomplete entity information.
rules.fix: Declare the type as an entity here too (Kind Key / Extend / Reference with the same @key).

rules.title: A field has the same type in every subgraph
rules.message: has a different type in another subgraph — field types should be identical across subgraphs.
rules.fix: Use exactly the same type (including ! and list wrappers) in every subgraph that defines the field.

rules.title: A field has the same arguments in every subgraph
rules.message: has arguments that are missing in another subgraph that defines the same field — they are dropped from the supergraph.
rules.fix: Declare the same arguments on the field in every subgraph.

rules.title: An argument has the same type in every subgraph
rules.message: has an argument whose type differs from another subgraph's definition of the same field.
rules.fix: Use exactly the same argument type (including !) in every subgraph.

rules.title: Argument defaults are consistent
rules.message: has an argument with a default value in one subgraph but not in another.
rules.fix: Give the argument the same default value in every subgraph (or none in all).

rules.title: A type has the same description in every subgraph
rules.message: has a different description in another subgraph.
rules.fix: Use one description for the type in every subgraph (or describe it only in the owning subgraph).

rules.title: Input enums have the same values in every subgraph
rules.message: is used as an input and its values differ from another subgraph — only the shared values reach the supergraph.
rules.fix: Define the same enum values in every subgraph that declares the enum.

rules.title: Output enums have the same values in every subgraph
rules.message: has values that differ from another subgraph — all values are merged into the supergraph.
rules.fix: Define the same enum values in every subgraph that declares the enum.

rules.title: Input types have the same fields in every subgraph
rules.message: has fields that another subgraph's definition of the same input does not — they are dropped from the supergraph.
rules.fix: Define the same input fields in every subgraph that declares the input type.

rules.title: Value types have the same fields in every subgraph
rules.message: is a value type (no @key) whose fields differ from another subgraph's definition.
rules.fix: Define the same fields for the value type in every subgraph, or make it an entity.

rules.title: Interfaces have the same fields in every subgraph
rules.message: is an interface whose fields differ from another subgraph's definition.
rules.fix: Define the same interface fields in every subgraph.

rules.title: Finish progressive @override migrations
rules.section: Composition rules › Overridden and unused elements
rules.message: uses @override with a label — a progressive field migration is still in progress.
rules.fix: Complete the migration, then remove the label (and later the @override).

rules.title: Remove @override once the source field is gone
rules.section: Composition rules › Overridden and unused elements
rules.message: has @override(from: …) but the source subgraph no longer defines the field.
rules.fix: Remove the @override directive.

rules.title: Remove fields another subgraph overrides
rules.section: Composition rules › Overridden and unused elements
rules.message: is fully overridden by another subgraph (@override without a label), so it is never resolved here.
rules.fix: Remove the field from this subgraph (keep it only if another field's @requires/@key needs it, then mark it @external).

rules.title: @override names an existing subgraph
rules.message: has @override(from: …) naming a subgraph that does not exist in the registry.
rules.fix: Correct the subgraph name (Business Application) or remove the @override.

rules.title: Every enum is used
rules.section: Composition rules › Overridden and unused elements
rules.message: is defined but no field, argument or operation in any subgraph references it.
rules.fix: Reference the enum or remove it.

rules.title: Unions have the same members in every subgraph
rules.message: union member types should be the same in every subgraph that defines the union.
rules.fix: Define the same union members in every subgraph.

rules.title: @shareable fields return the same runtime types
rules.message: a @shareable field's abstract return type should resolve to the same runtime types in every subgraph.
rules.fix: Make the interface/union implementations identical across the subgraphs sharing the field.

rules.title: Executable directives are defined in every subgraph
rules.message: an executable directive should be defined in every subgraph.
rules.fix: Add the directive definition to every subgraph.

rules.title: Executable directive locations match
rules.message: an executable directive should declare the same locations in every subgraph.
rules.fix: Use the same `on …` locations in every definition of the directive.

rules.title: Executable directive repeatability matches
rules.message: an executable directive should be repeatable in all subgraphs or none.
rules.fix: Make `repeatable` consistent across subgraphs.

rules.title: Type-system directive locations match
rules.message: a type-system directive should declare the same locations in every subgraph.
rules.fix: Use the same `on …` locations in every definition of the directive.

rules.title: Type-system directive repeatability matches
rules.message: a type-system directive should be repeatable in all subgraphs or none.
rules.fix: Make `repeatable` consistent across subgraphs.

rules.title: Non-repeatable directive arguments match
rules.message: a non-repeatable directive applied to the same element should use the same arguments in every subgraph.
rules.fix: Use identical directive arguments across subgraphs.

rules.title: Merged non-repeatable directive arguments
rules.message: a non-repeatable directive's differing arguments were merged during composition.
rules.fix: Align the directive arguments across subgraphs.

rules.title: Executable directive locations overlap
rules.message: an executable directive has no location common to every subgraph, so it is dropped from the supergraph.
rules.fix: Give the directive at least one shared location in every subgraph.

rules.title: Custom directive composition
rules.message: a custom directive composed via @composeDirective has an issue.
rules.fix: Check the @composeDirective / @link declarations in each subgraph.
